s1.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: History of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT
Acute injury to the orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI
Cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as Streptococcus pyogenes

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: History of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT
Acute injury to the orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI
Cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as Streptococcus pyogenes

shortlist.label: Orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of orbital pain, edema, and hyperemia

shortlist.label: Lacrimal sac abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging confirmed left-sided lacrimal sac abscess

shortlist.label: Subperiosteal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Postseptal fat stranding and globe compression on CT

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements and vision loss

shortlist.label: Orbital apex syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute injury to the orbital segment of the left optic nerve on MRI

raw.rationale: The presence of a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT, along with postseptal fat stranding and the patient's history of epiphora, strongly supports this diagnosis. The cultures isolating Streptococcus pyogenes also suggest an infectious cause, consistent with an abscess.

rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: While the patient has signs of orbital inflammation, the specific finding of a lacrimal sac abscess points to a more localized infection.

rejected.label: Subperiosteal abscess
rejected.why: There is no mention of an abscess along the orbital bones, which would be characteristic of a subperiosteal abscess.

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings do not suggest involvement of the cavernous sinus, such as bilateral eye involvement or specific mention of sinus thrombosis.

rejected.label: Orbital apex syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically involves multiple cranial nerves and has a more severe presentation, which is not fully consistent with the patient's symptoms and findings.
